faqs.q: Which flat-roof membrane is best for an Orange Valley Arts loft or commercial building?

runs.v: It depends: white TPO reflects heat for energy efficiency on sun-exposed roofs, EPDM brings durability as single-ply coverage, and modified bitumen adds a tough multi-ply surface.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a flat roof on an Orange commercial or multi-family building?

runs.v: Often. Under the 25% rule of N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, part of the Uniform Construction Code that regulates roof permits, repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building needs one, while re-covering a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance. Installs follow local construction codes, and a full replacement or substantial repair means coordination with local building inspectors; confirm with the City of Orange Township construction office.

faqs.q: Why does my flat roof keep leaking despite repeated patches?

runs.v: Patches trap moisture and shift drainage, so ponding forms away from the drains. A full roof replacement with a new roof membrane and tapered insulation ends the cycle, and addressing small issues promptly prevents larger, costlier repairs.

faqs.q: Does a flat roof in an Orange historic district need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. Confirm the property's local historic status with the City of Orange Township before exterior work; a Register listing alone imposes no restriction.

faqs.q: How do you handle a flat-roof repair on a tenant-occupied Orange rental?
